messages:
alertbot: ALERT: route /v1/stream p99=2200ms (SLO=1500ms) on shared-pool-3. Auto-page @oncall-sre. severity=high :rotating_light:

mia: grabbing traces. saw big tail starting ~15:12 UTC, coincides with host gpu-03-04 write spike. streaming frames queueing.

leo: logs show repeated 'kvcache_evict -> disk_read' on runtime; stack shows io wait spikes. attaching quick grep: `grep -E \"kvcache|evict|disk_read\" /var/log/inference/runtime.log | tail -n 50`

infra-bot: sample output pasted: ```
[15:12:02] kvcache: evict key=0x7f8a size=12MB reason=mem_pressure
[15:12:03] storage: disk_read latency=320ms path=/mnt/nvme0/models
[15:12:04] runtime: stream stall detected conn=abc123 wait=420ms
```

kat: looks like tenant with id=9002 (label=heavy-io-tenant) is doing large background checkpoint writes. cgroup blkio stats show write_bw=38MB/s for cgroup 9002 over 30s windows.

oncall-sre: oncall here. do we have an immediate mitigation that doesn't risk data loss?

mia: quick options: 1) throttle cgroup write bps, 2) move tenant off this pool to pool-11, 3) raise runtime KV cache size (memory constrained), 4) graceful reject new long-running streaming sessions for that tenant. prefer migration + temporary throttle.

ops: we have an idle spare in pool-11 with ~40% headroom. migration command: `rwd-tenant move 9002 --to pool-11 --grace 20s --allow-concurrent`

infra-bot: running `iostat -xnv 1 3` shows: ```
Device            r/s   w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s  await  svctm %util
nvme0n1         0.10 420.00   4k  42800   5.2    0.20  87.5
```

kat: that's sustained nvme write util high. immediate throttle to 25MB/s: 
```
echo "253:0 9002 25000000" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device || true
```

leo: applied throttle. disk write dropped ~60% in 12s. p99 decreased from 2200ms -> 1400ms (still borderline).

ops: kick off tenant move with canary: `rwd-tenant move 9002 --to pool-11 --grace 20s --percent 10`

mia: starting route-level fallback for streaming to non-stream for tenant 9002 at 5% of traffic to reduce user-visible stalls during migration: 
```
redwoodctl route set /v1/stream --fallback /v1/generate-sync --match tenant=9002 --percent=5
```

oncall-sre: monitoring p95/p99 and NVMe util on both source and dest pools.

ops: migration canary progressed 10% -> 100% over 3 minutes, no errors. pool-11 nvme util remains <30%.

infra-bot: summary metrics after migration+throttle+fallback: p95=380ms, p99=820ms. request error rate unchanged.

leo: note: we saw a subtle race where KV cache eviction triggered model shard reloads increasing disk reads; runtime should rate-limit shard reloads to avoid cascading io. adding to follow-ups.

kat: customer impact: affected tenant experienced stalls on long-lived streams for ~9 minutes, auto-fallback engaged for ~5% sessions. no failed writes.

oncall-sre: good work. next steps: 1) create automated rule to detect sustained blkio write > 20MB/s AND p99 > SLO for 60s to auto-trigger containment, 2) add soft limit policy for checkpointing jobs (ops) to schedule outside heavy traffic, 3) implement KV cache eviction low-latency path to avoid disk reads. assign owners.

mia: posting logs to incidents bucket: s3://incidents/1795550000/runtime-logs.tar.gz and a heap of perf traces.

ops: filing temporary alert adjustment so ops don't fat-fail on small, recovered blips.

oncall-sre: handing off to infra rotation for deep root cause. Ill draft a postmortem and link here. thanks team. :thumbsup:

alertbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (throttle, migration, fallback). current status=monitoring.

ops: quick runbook note: command snippets used (throttle, move, route fallback) added to /runbooks/noisy-io-tenant.md draft. owner=kat.

mia: closing timeline: total impact window ~12 minutes, p99 breach lasted ~10 minutes. final p99 back to 700ms.

alertbot: INCIDENT CLOSED - final_status=resolved. tags=[noisy-neighbor, blkio, kvcache-evict, migration, streaming].

kat: follow-ups queued in #postmortems. will include customer notice template for tenants that run heavy checkpoint jobs during peak hours.
